title: CLAUDE.md
text: Never duplicate parameter docs. Always use @inheritParams pointing function already documents parameters:

title: CLAUDE.md
text: ruthlessly concise. Max two sentences per block (title/description, @param, @return). ;. em dash (see ). State thing , doesn’t every edge case — put @details instead. @param lines follow structure, {...} placeholder actual type/value (literal braces): Example: @param name String. Name new class.
code: @param name Value type. Concise definition.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Always use rlang standalone checks every parameter function. imported via R/import-standalone-types-check.R:
code: check_string(x, allow_empty = FALSE) check_bool(x) check_number_whole(x, min = 1, max = 100) check_number_decimal(x) check_character(x, allow_null = TRUE) check_data_frame(x) check_function(x)

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Use cli::cli_abort() call = error_call (call = rlang::caller_env()). Use cli inline markup: {.arg x}, {.cls ClassName}, {.fn function_name}, {.val value}, {.code expr}. S7 validator messages (string returned class validator = function(self) {...}) don’t go cli_abort() since S7 pastes bullets verbatim. Build cli::format_inline() instead sprintf()/paste(), using inline markup, e.g.:
code: cli::format_inline("@value must be one of {.val {self@variants}}")

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Prefer rlang equivalent base R function one exists. particular, use rlang::expr() instead quote() capturing unevaluated expressions (e.g. S7::new_property() promise defaults).

title: CLAUDE.md

what: Extensions to the S7 Object System
title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: s7x provides utility extensions {S7} type system. fills void features ’ve long wanted S7 (R) help make R packages type safe(ish) less boilerplate. Notably s7x provides: extensible Enum class speficying enumerations scalar properties arrays S7 classes range propeties (discrete continuous) property intersections See Enums R: towards type safe R motivation behind package.

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: can install development version s7x like : [!NOTE] s7x built development version S7. Install pak::pak("RConsortium/S7").
code: pak::pak("josiahparry/s7x")

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: R, use enumerations time, though formally. example, stats::cor()’s argument method = c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman") enumeration method can one three possible values. R, enums typically strings validated via arg.match() equivalent rlang::arg_match(). s7x, enums formalized s7x::Enum class. Note s7x::Enums can cast character vectors. Thus, can use Enum enforce variants, need underlying value can .character() extract ’s value via x@value.
code: library(s7x)  # create a new enum CorMethod <- new_enum("CorMethod", c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman"))  # instantiate the enum x <- CorMethod("pearson") x #> <CorMethod> #>  @ value   : chr "pearson" #>  @ variants: chr [1:3] "pearson" "kendall" "spearman" #>  @ allow_na: logi TRUE as.character(x) #> [1] "pearson"

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: longtime wish list item mine scalar properties. scalar R length one vector. useful arguments n_components = 5—wouldn’t make sense value c(5, 1), example. S7 built-classes vector types R (double, integer, character, list) scalar variants. s7x introduces property_scalar() function lets create scalar variants. example: Providing non-length 1 value creates error:
code: library(S7) NComponents := new_class(   properties = list(n = property_scalar(S7::class_integer)) )  n_comps <- NComponents(5L) n_comps #> <NComponents> #>  @ n: int 5 NComponents(c(5L, 1L)) #> Error in `NComponents()`: #> ! <NComponents> object properties are invalid: #> - @n must be a scalar atomic

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: example, wanted model chess board: can combine enum normal S7 object define position chess piece.
code: Rank := new_class(   properties = list(number = property_range_discrete(1, 8, allow_na = FALSE)) )  File := new_class(   properties = list(number = property_range_discrete(1, 8, allow_na = FALSE)) ) Piece := new_enum(   c("Pawn", "Bishop", "Knight", "Rook", "Queen", "King"),   allow_na = FALSE,   default = "Pawn" )  Square := new_class(   properties = list(     piece = Piece,     rank = Rank,     file = File   ) )  queen_start <- Square(   Piece("Queen"),   Rank(1L),   File(4L) )  queen_start #> <Square> #>  @ piece: <Piece> #>  .. @ value   : chr "Queen" #>  .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" "Queen" "King" #>  .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE #>  @ rank : <Rank> #>  .. @ number: int 1 #>  @ file : <File> #>  .. @ number: int 4

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: Often, may want contain array S7 objects. property_array() gives us strongly typed arrays S7 objects. wanted record position player’s pieces turn create new type contains array Squares.
code: PlayerPieces := new_class(   properties = list(pieces = property_array(Square)) )  white <- PlayerPieces(   list(     queen_start,     Square(       Piece("King"),       Rank(1L),       File(5L)     )   ) )  white #> <PlayerPieces> #>  @ pieces: List of 2 #>  .. $ : <Square> #>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece> #>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "Queen" #>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ... #>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE #>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1 #>  ..  ..@ file : <File> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 4 #>  .. $ : <Square> #>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece> #>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "King" #>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ... #>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE #>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1 #>  ..  ..@ file : <File> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 5

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: s7x package introduces generics as_vector() from_vector() provide conversion methods base S3 vectors types list, character vector, etc. defualt implementation following: S7 objects: creates named list property value Enums: converts character vector Ranges: converts double integer can create bespoke methods well. example, can use as_vector() convert Square() list. Additionally, data comes format list another type, can parse correct S7 type using from_vector(object, S7_class).
code: queen_list <- as_vector(queen_start) queen_list #> $piece #> [1] "Queen" #>  #> $rank #> $rank$number #> [1] 1 #>  #>  #> $file #> $file$number #> [1] 4 round_tripped <- from_vector(queen_list, Square) round_tripped #> <Square> #>  @ piece: <Piece> #>  .. @ value   : chr "Queen" #>  .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" "Queen" "King" #>  .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE #>  @ rank : <Rank> #>  .. @ number: int 1 #>  @ file : <File> #>  .. @ number: int 4  # verify no differences waldo::compare(queen_start, round_tripped) #> ✔ No differences

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: Inspired serde serde_json rust ecosystem, s7x provides generics from_json() to_json(). use yyjsonr hood fast performance. Now, can call from_json() parse back correct type. particularly useful property_array() want list S7 class:
code: to_json(white, pretty = TRUE) |>   cat() #> { #>   "pieces": [ #>     { #>       "piece": "Queen", #>       "rank": { #>         "number": 1 #>       }, #>       "file": { #>         "number": 4 #>       } #>     }, #>     { #>       "piece": "King", #>       "rank": { #>         "number": 1 #>       }, #>       "file": { #>         "number": 5 #>       } #>     } #>   ] #> } # round trip the json conversion to_json(white) |>   from_json(PlayerPieces) #> <PlayerPieces> #>  @ pieces: List of 2 #>  .. $ : <Square> #>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece> #>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "Queen" #>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ... #>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE #>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1 #>  ..  ..@ file : <File> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 4 #>  .. $ : <Square> #>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece> #>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "King" #>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ... #>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE #>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1 #>  ..  ..@ file : <File> #>  .. .. .. @ number: int 5

title: Convert S7 objects to and from vectors — as_vector
text: as_vector() returns: S7_object: named list coerced properties. Enum: value string. list: list S7 object bare list element coerced. leaves elements, data frames, unchanged. Falls back use .list(). from_vector() builds class properties x. returns atomic vectors unchanged unclasses data frames first.

title: Convert S7 objects to and from vectors — as_vector
